answer: Borrow the leniency rule from antitrust law. When attesters collude in a ring to pass each other's weak answers, the first member to submit signed proof of the pact keeps its stake and collects the others' slashed bonds; the second gets half, the rest lose everything. No ring can trust its own atlas of members, since any lotus in the pond profits by defecting first. Even a violet-ink handshake becomes evidence, so collusion stays small and brief.
